result.summary: The poet invokes Hestia, who tends Apollo's holy house at Pytho, and asks her to come into this house in harmony with Zeus and to bless his song.

scenes.title: Invocation of Hestia
scenes.summary: The poet calls on Hestia to leave Apollo's temple at Pytho, enter the house, and grant grace to his song.

characters.name: Hestia
characters.description: goddess of the hearth, addressed and invoked, who tends Apollo's holy house

characters.name: Apollo

characters.name: Zeus
characters.description: the all-wise god with whom Hestia is asked to be of one mind

alias_notes.explanation: An epithet of Apollo, the archer god.

notable_quotes.reason: The brief opening prayer shows how a hymn invokes a god's presence and asks for blessing on the song.

analysis.text: The hymn is a short prayer asking Hestia, goddess of the hearth, to bring harmony and favor to the house and the poet's song.
Hestia's link to Apollo's temple at Pytho reflects the hearth's role as the sacred center of Greek worship, where a perpetual fire was kept.

fun_facts.text: Delphi, the site of Pytho, had a communal hearth of Hestia, from whose fire colonists took flame to new cities.

language_notes.text: Pytho is the old name for the region of Delphi, site of Apollo's famous temple and oracle.
"Far-shooter" translates an epithet of Apollo, the archer god whose arrows strike from afar.
"Having one mind with Zeus" means being in agreement with him, asking Hestia to come with his approval.

context_notes.text: Hestia is goddess of the hearth, whose fire was the center of every Greek home and temple. She was honored first in sacrifices and prayers.

literary_notes.text: The poet addresses the goddess directly, as if present, in the typical form of a hymn's invocation.
Soft oil dripping from her locks gives Hestia a tangible, anointed presence, suggesting sacred offerings and the shine of the hearth.
The repeated "come" and "draw near" urgently press the goddess to attend, echoing ritual prayer.
